Let black \(=1\), white \(=0\). For every unit triangle, the rule is equivalent to the sum of its three vertex colors being \(1\pmod 2\).

Let \(n=2022\). Use coordinates \((i,j)\) with \(i,j\ge 0\), \(i+j\le n\). For a rhombus formed by one upward and one downward unit triangle, their parity equations are
\[
x_{i,j}+x_{i+1,j}+x_{i,j+1}=1,
\]
\[
x_{i+1,j}+x_{i,j+1}+x_{i+1,j+1}=1.
\]
Adding gives
\[
x_{i,j}=x_{i+1,j+1}.
\]
Thus the color is constant along diagonals \(i-j=d\). Let \(y_d\) be the color on diagonal \(d\).

For an upward triangle, the diagonals involved are \(d-1,d,d+1\), so
\[
y_{d-1}+y_d+y_{d+1}=1.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
y_{d+1}=1+y_d+y_{d-1}.
\]
Over \(\mathbb F_2\), the homogeneous recurrence has period \(3\), so every solution is periodic with period \(3\). Therefore the whole coloring is determined by any two consecutive diagonal colors, giving
\[
2^2=4
\]
possible patterns.

\[
\boxed{4}
\]
